displayName: Full Software Lifecycle with CIM → PIM → PSM

roles.name: Product Owner
responsibilities: Owns product outcomes, priority, release scope, and acceptance decisions

roles.name: Delivery Lead
responsibilities: Maintains the integrated process run, dependency board, risks, cadence, and impediment escalation

roles.name: Business Modeler
responsibilities: Leads CIM discovery and domain-model increments

roles.name: Requirements Engineer
responsibilities: Maintains requirements, acceptance criteria, and change impact evidence

roles.name: Domain Expert
responsibilities: Validates business language, rules, and operational fit

roles.name: Solution Architect
responsibilities: Leads PIM architecture, contracts, integration, and cross-level decisions

roles.name: Cloud Platform Engineer
responsibilities: Leads AWS PSM, generation, environments, and platform automation

roles.name: Quality Engineer
responsibilities: Owns verification strategy, evidence quality, and quality risks

roles.name: Security Engineer
responsibilities: Owns security, privacy, threat, and exception evidence

roles.name: Release Engineer
responsibilities: Owns release candidates, promotion, rollback, and deployment records

roles.name: Service Owner
responsibilities: Accepts operational readiness, SLOs, support ownership, and service outcomes

roles.name: Process Reviewer
responsibilities: Reviews gates, evidence, decisions, and method improvement

roles.name: Method Engineer
responsibilities: Tailors and evolves the situational method and its process assets

artifactKinds.name: Product and System Charter
artifactKinds.description: Product goal, outcome hypothesis, scope boundaries, constraints, and success measures.

artifactKinds.name: Situational Method Profile
artifactKinds.description: Tailored lifecycle, roles, work products, gates, evidence rules, and metrics for the project context.

artifactKinds.name: Team Topology and Dependency Map
artifactKinds.description: Team ownership, interfaces, dependency board, decision rights, and coordination cadence.

artifactKinds.name: Increment Record
artifactKinds.description: Slice goal, scope, acceptance evidence, model revisions, transformation runs, and retrospective results.

artifactKinds.name: Release Record
artifactKinds.description: Release scope, exact model and artifact revisions, approvals, deployment evidence, rollback identity, and outcome.

artifactKinds.name: Operations and Learning Record
artifactKinds.description: SLOs, incidents, changes, product outcomes, and method-improvement actions.

artifactKinds.name: Retirement and Closure Record
artifactKinds.description: Retirement decision, migration/data disposition, decommission evidence, and retained knowledge.

guidelines.name: Thin vertical increments
guidelines.text: Deliver one capability slice through CIM → PIM → PSM → artifact readiness per engine revolution. The engine repeats inside release, operations, and retirement lifecycle governance; avoid big-bang modeling.

guidelines.name: Human-in-the-loop transforms
guidelines.text: ETL and M2T are assistive. ManualDecision and readiness gates block promotion when automation is uncertain.

guidelines.name: Empirical process control
guidelines.text: Plan a small vertical slice, inspect executable model evidence at each gate, and adapt the backlog after artifact review.

sourceOfTruth: The project work tracker stores one process-run record per increment or release candidate.
The model repository stores the model revision, transformation run, validation evidence, and readiness assessment.
The release record stores the exact accepted model, generator, artifact, test, and deployment revisions.

aggregation.rule: Aggregate by increment, team, release, and product; never average away a blocking finding.
aggregation.teamCoordination: Publish a shared dependency board with ownership, dependency type, due date, and escalation path.
aggregation.reviewCadence: Daily local coordination, per-increment review/retrospective, and per-release readiness review.

metrics.name: Eligible task completion
metrics.cadence: each workday and at gate review
metrics.interpretation: Visibility only; never substitute for a usable increment.

metrics.name: Increment flow time
metrics.interpretation: Use trends to tune slice size and expose queues.

metrics.name: Rework rate
metrics.formula: reopened tasks caused by a finding / completed tasks
metrics.interpretation: Inspect causes; do not use as an individual performance score.

metrics.name: Trace coverage
metrics.formula: accepted scope items with source-to-evidence trace / accepted scope items
metrics.cadence: at every level gate and release
metrics.interpretation: A low value blocks confidence even when task completion is high.

metrics.name: Open blocking findings
metrics.interpretation: Must be zero or covered by an explicit, time-bound risk acceptance.

metrics.name: Manual decision closure
metrics.formula: accepted/rejected/waived manual decisions / blocking manual decisions
metrics.interpretation: Open decisions remain visible and are not silently treated as done.

metrics.name: Accepted vertical-slice rate
metrics.interpretation: A slice is accepted only when it is usable and all required evidence exists.

metrics.name: Cross-team dependency age
metrics.formula: now - openedAt for the oldest unresolved dependency
metrics.interpretation: Escalate aging dependencies before they become integration surprises.

metrics.name: Release frequency
metrics.interpretation: Interpret with change failure rate, recovery time, and product outcomes.

governance.gate: The end-to-end method coordinates the child processes; it does not waive any level gate or the artifact/release process.

processEngine.description: One vertical CIM → PIM → PSM → artifact-readiness revolution per capability increment, embedded in release, operations, and retirement governance.

deliverable.name: Deployable increment
deliverable.description: Accepted models at all levels, generated artifacts, verification evidence, and an explicit increment decision for one slice.

loop.guidance: After increment acceptance, either start the next capability slice or leave the engine for release assembly. Any downstream finding re-enters the smallest affected child process through the recorded change workflow.

reworkLoops.name: PIM Discovery Feedback to CIM
reworkLoops.trigger: PIM refinement reveals missing CIM concepts for the increment.
reworkLoops.guidance: Extend CIM via change workflow; re-run CIM EVL before re-transform.

reworkLoops.name: PSM Platform Feedback to PIM
reworkLoops.trigger: AWS constraints require PIM architecture changes.
reworkLoops.guidance: Adjust PIM policies or integration; re-run PIM→PSM ETL.

reworkLoops.name: M2T Artifact Feedback to PSM
reworkLoops.trigger: Generated artifacts fail validation or deployment dry-run.
reworkLoops.guidance: Fix PSM at source stage; regenerate artifacts.

phases.name: Initiate, Tailor & Organize
phases.objective: Establish the product/system purpose, situational method, team topology, quality baseline, and release strategy before modeling begins.
entryCriteria: A problem, opportunity, or mandated change has an accountable sponsor
exitCriteria: The method profile is approved
Teams, ownership, dependencies, and decision rights are explicit
The first increment has a testable outcome hypothesis
phases.tailoringNote: Tailor by risk, novelty, regulatory exposure, team distribution, and architecture volatility; retain evidence and gate obligations even when activities are combined.

stages.name: Product and System Intent
stages.objective: Turn the opportunity into an outcome-oriented product/system charter and release hypothesis.

tasks.name: Define product outcomes and success measures
steps: State the user or mission problem and desired outcomes.
Define measurable product, operational, security, and quality outcomes.
Record assumptions, constraints, non-goals, and the first release hypothesis.
exitCriteria: Outcome measures and non-goals are accepted by stakeholders
validationRules: Every initial scope item is connected to an outcome or mandatory constraint
tasks.progressEvidence: Define product outcomes and success measures decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis
steps: Identify the smallest useful vertical capability slice.
Define acceptance signals and the evidence needed to call it usable.
Record unresolved assumptions as owned decisions rather than hidden risks.
exitCriteria: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis evidence is recorded
validationRules: The first slice crosses the required lifecycle boundary and has observable acceptance evidence
tasks.progressEvidence: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Situational Method Tailoring
stages.objective: Select and tailor method fragments to the project context without removing essential control objectives.

tasks.name: Assess context and method risks
steps: Assess criticality, regulatory obligations, novelty, uncertainty, team distribution, system size, and delivery cadence.
Select the required CIM, PIM, PSM, artifact, and lifecycle activities.
Record excluded, combined, or delegated activities with rationale and compensating evidence.
exitCriteria: Assess context and method risks evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every tailoring decision names its context, consequence, owner, and review point
tasks.progressEvidence: Assess context and method risks decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done
steps: Define entry and exit evidence for model slices, transformations, release candidates, and operations.
Define which findings are blocking and how time-bound risk acceptance works.
Publish the profile version used by the process run.
exitCriteria: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done evidence is recorded
validationRules: A task cannot be accepted solely because activity occurred; required evidence and gate criteria are explicit
tasks.progressEvidence: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Team Topology & Coordination
stages.objective: Make ownership and coordination explicit for multiple teams working on one integrated model and product.

tasks.name: Define team ownership and interfaces
steps: Partition work by bounded capability, service, platform concern, or lifecycle responsibility.
Assign model ownership, repository ownership, decision rights, and backup owners.
Define interface contracts and the shared dependency board.
exitCriteria: Define team ownership and interfaces evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every owned model scope has one accountable owner and a named integration path
tasks.progressEvidence: Define team ownership and interfaces decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths
steps: Set local team syncs, cross-team integration reviews, increment reviews, release reviews, and retrospectives.
Define escalation thresholds for aging dependencies, blocking findings, and conflicting model ownership.
Define how concurrent model edits are merged, reviewed, and reconciled.
exitCriteria: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths evidence is recorded
validationRules: Coordination events produce decisions, dependency status, and evidence links
tasks.progressEvidence: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Quality, Security & Operations Baseline
stages.objective: Set cross-cutting quality, security, operational, and release constraints before design detail accumulates.

tasks.name: Define quality and security control objectives
steps: Identify privacy, threat, compliance, resilience, performance, accessibility, and audit obligations.
Map control objectives to model evidence, generated artifact evidence, and explicit human decisions.
Set severity and blocking policies.
exitCriteria: Define quality and security control objectives evidence is recorded
validationRules: Critical controls have an accountable owner and verification evidence path
tasks.progressEvidence: Define quality and security control objectives decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Define operational and release strategy
steps: Define environments, support ownership, SLO hypotheses, observability expectations, rollback posture, and release cadence.
Identify data migration, compatibility, and progressive-delivery constraints.
Record the initial release decision policy.
exitCriteria: Define operational and release strategy evidence is recorded
validationRules: The release strategy names promotion, rollback, and post-deployment validation evidence
tasks.progressEvidence: Define operational and release strategy decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

phases.name: Iterative-Incremental Model-Driven Delivery
phases.objective: Deliver usable vertical increments by coordinating CIM, PIM, PSM, transformation, generation, and artifact-readiness child processes.
entryCriteria: A tailored method profile and team topology exist
An increment goal and acceptance hypothesis are ready
exitCriteria: The increment is accepted, deferred with explicit rationale, or returned for bounded rework
The increment record contains model, transformation, artifact, and acceptance evidence
phases.tailoringNote: The engine is the repeatable kernel. Teams may work concurrently inside a cycle, but promotion remains evidence-based and downstream work cannot silently accept unresolved upstream decisions.

stages.name: Frame Increment
stages.objective: Select a thin, valuable, testable capability slice and establish its evidence plan.

tasks.name: Plan the vertical increment
steps: Select scope from the ordered product backlog.
Define outcome, acceptance criteria, dependencies, risks, and expected model/artifact evidence.
Assign scope items to owning teams and establish the increment ledger.
exitCriteria: Increment scope, owners, acceptance evidence, and dependencies are agreed
validationRules: The slice is small enough to inspect end-to-end and large enough to demonstrate a user or operational outcome
tasks.progressEvidence: Plan the vertical increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: CIM Child Process
stages.objective: Refine business intent and domain behavior for the selected slice.

tasks.name: Run the CIM increment
steps: Execute the CIM process for the selected capability slice.
Record semantic decisions, assumptions, trace links, readiness findings, and accepted CIM revision.
Return unresolved cross-team or product decisions to the integrated decision register.
exitCriteria: CIM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: Assistant-applied model changes pass structural Ecore/EMF conformance; semantic validation remains an explicit user/model validation workflow
tasks.progressEvidence: Run the CIM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: CIM → PIM Transformation
stages.objective: Transform the accepted CIM revision into PIM scaffolding while preserving traceability and surfacing manual decisions.

tasks.name: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation
steps: Pin the source CIM revision and transformation profile.
Run the transformation and inspect report, trace links, assumptions, and manual decisions.
Accept, reject, or route each material decision and record the target PIM revision.
exitCriteria: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every generated target scope item is traceable to a source or explicit transformation decision
tasks.progressEvidence: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: PIM Child Process
stages.objective: Refine service boundaries, contracts, data, behavior, integration, assurance, and platform intent.

tasks.name: Run the PIM increment
steps: Execute the PIM process for the transformed slice.
Review contracts, data access, integration, policy, platform mapping, and operational assumptions.
Record accepted PIM revision and open platform decisions.
exitCriteria: PIM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: Generated PIM is treated as scaffolding until the solution architect accepts material decisions
tasks.progressEvidence: Run the PIM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: PIM → AWS PSM Transformation
stages.objective: Map accepted platform-independent architecture to AWS-specific deployment intent.

tasks.name: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation
steps: Pin the source PIM revision and AWS mapping profile.
Run the transformation and inspect resource mappings, assumptions, security implications, and trace links.
Record accepted target PSM revision or route mapping gaps back to PIM.
exitCriteria: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every deployable PIM scope item has an accepted AWS mapping or a documented exception
tasks.progressEvidence: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: PSM Child Process
stages.objective: Refine AWS resources, relationships, security, observability, and deployment readiness for the slice.

tasks.name: Run the PSM increment
steps: Execute the AWS PSM process for the transformed slice.
Review resource relationships, IAM, networking, data, eventing, APIs, workflows, and operational views.
Record accepted PSM revision and unresolved deployment risks.
exitCriteria: PSM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: AWS platform choices are traceable to accepted PIM intent or explicit platform decisions
tasks.progressEvidence: Run the PSM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Model-to-Text Generation
stages.objective: Generate a reproducible artifact baseline from the accepted PSM revision.

tasks.name: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline
steps: Pin PSM revision, generator version, templates, and environment profile.
Generate application, infrastructure, configuration, tests, and documentation artifacts.
Record the generation manifest and route structural gaps to PSM or generator ownership.
exitCriteria: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline evidence is recorded
validationRules: The generated baseline is reproducible from recorded inputs and contains no secret material
tasks.progressEvidence: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Increment Readiness & Acceptance
stages.objective: Verify the exact generated candidate, capture acceptance evidence, and decide whether the increment is usable, reworkable, or deferred.

tasks.name: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment
steps: Execute the artifact deployment-readiness process for the generated candidate.
Review verification, security, rollback, operational, and acceptance evidence.
Record increment outcome, open findings, deferred scope, and feedback loops for the next cycle.
exitCriteria: Increment is accepted, explicitly deferred, or returned through a named rework loop
validationRules: No blocking finding is silently closed; risk acceptance is explicit, owned, time-bound, and traceable
tasks.progressEvidence: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

phases.name: Release & Transition
phases.objective: Assemble accepted increments into a controlled release, promote progressively, validate in the target environment, and hand over operational ownership.
entryCriteria: Release scope is composed of accepted increments
Artifact, security, quality, and operations evidence is available
exitCriteria: Release outcome is recorded
Service ownership and rollback posture are accepted
Post-deployment validation is complete

stages.name: Release Train Assembly
stages.objective: Compose and verify a release from accepted increment records.

tasks.name: Assemble the release candidate
steps: Select accepted increments and compatible model/artifact revisions.
Resolve cross-team dependency and compatibility checks.
Create the release record with exact inputs and promotion sequence.
exitCriteria: Assemble the release candidate evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every release scope item maps to an accepted increment and exact artifact identity
tasks.progressEvidence: Assemble the release candidate decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria
steps: Inspect readiness assessments, validation results, security exceptions, rollback plan, operational runbooks, and approvals.
Confirm open blockers are zero or explicitly accepted under the tailored method profile.
Record the go/no-go decision and decision owners.
exitCriteria: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria evidence is recorded
validationRules: Go/no-go is evidence-based and not inferred from task completion
tasks.progressEvidence: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Progressive Promotion
stages.objective: Promote the release through environments with controlled observation and rollback readiness.

tasks.name: Deploy and validate progressively
steps: Deploy the exact candidate to the approved environment sequence.
Run smoke, functional, security, data, observability, and compatibility checks.
Compare observed outcomes with release acceptance signals and stop or roll back on threshold breach.
exitCriteria: Deploy and validate progressively evidence is recorded
validationRules: Promotion evidence identifies candidate, environment, timestamp, operator, and observed result
tasks.progressEvidence: Deploy and validate progressively decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal
steps: Verify dashboards, alerts, runbooks, escalation paths, support ownership, and recovery access.
Confirm rollback and data-recovery actions are usable for the release.
Accept operational ownership or return the release to rework.
exitCriteria: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal evidence is recorded
validationRules: Operational acceptance names an accountable service owner and recovery evidence
tasks.progressEvidence: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Release Review
stages.objective: Inspect release outcomes and feed product, process, and architecture learning back into the backlog.

tasks.name: Review release outcome and update roadmap
steps: Compare product and operational outcomes with the release hypothesis.
Accept outcomes, revise priorities, and create follow-up increments for gaps.
Record decisions and changes to scope, measures, and assumptions.
exitCriteria: Review release outcome and update roadmap evidence is recorded
validationRules: Outcome learning changes a backlog, product decision, or explicitly confirms the hypothesis
tasks.progressEvidence: Review release outcome and update roadmap decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

phases.name: Operate, Evolve & Learn
phases.objective: Operate the service, respond to incidents, evolve models and artifacts through controlled change propagation, and continuously improve the method.
entryCriteria: A service or operational capability has been released or is being maintained
exitCriteria: Operational work is recorded
Changes are traced through the appropriate lifecycle path
Product and method learning is reviewed at the agreed cadence

stages.name: Operate and Observe
stages.objective: Use operational evidence to assess service health, user outcomes, and control effectiveness.

tasks.name: Review SLOs, telemetry, and product outcomes
steps: Inspect service levels, errors, cost, security signals, usage, and product outcome measures.
Compare observations with the service and product hypotheses.
Create improvement or change items with evidence and owners.
exitCriteria: Review SLOs, telemetry, and product outcomes evidence is recorded
validationRules: Operational decisions are based on identified evidence and thresholds
tasks.progressEvidence: Review SLOs, telemetry, and product outcomes decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Incident, Problem & Risk Response
stages.objective: Restore service and address systemic causes while preserving traceability and learning.

tasks.name: Manage incidents and recovery
steps: Triage impact, stabilize service, communicate status, and execute approved recovery actions.
Record incident timeline, affected scope, decisions, and evidence.
Open problem, security, or change work for systemic causes.
exitCriteria: Manage incidents and recovery evidence is recorded
validationRules: Recovery and customer impact are recorded before closure
tasks.progressEvidence: Manage incidents and recovery decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Perform problem and risk learning
steps: Analyze contributing causes across requirements, models, transformation, generation, deployment, and operation.
Update controls, tests, model patterns, process guidance, or method profile as appropriate.
Review changes at the next increment or release boundary.
exitCriteria: Perform problem and risk learning evidence is recorded
validationRules: The corrective action is routed to the earliest responsible source rather than only patched downstream
tasks.progressEvidence: Perform problem and risk learning decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Change Propagation
stages.objective: Evolve the product through a controlled impact-analysis and re-execution path.

tasks.name: Assess and propagate a change
steps: Classify the change as product, domain, architecture, platform, artifact, operational, or retirement scope.
Use traces and dependency ownership to identify impacted downstream levels and teams.
Re-enter the smallest affected process stage, regenerate or redeploy as required, and preserve compatibility evidence.
exitCriteria: Assess and propagate a change evidence is recorded
validationRules: The change record identifies source revision, impacted levels, downstream evidence, and acceptance decision
tasks.progressEvidence: Assess and propagate a change decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Method and Product Retrospective
stages.objective: Improve the product and the method using evidence from increments, releases, incidents, and dependencies.

tasks.name: Inspect flow, quality, and coordination metrics
steps: Review flow time, rework, trace coverage, blockers, dependency age, escaped defects, and product outcomes.
Look for systemic queues, missing work products, invalid gates, and coordination failures.
Approve bounded method changes and record their expected effect.
exitCriteria: Inspect flow, quality, and coordination metrics evidence is recorded
validationRules: Metrics lead to inspectable improvement experiments rather than individual performance rankings
tasks.progressEvidence: Inspect flow, quality, and coordination metrics decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

phases.name: Retire, Migrate & Close
phases.objective: Retire a product or service safely, preserve required knowledge and evidence, and close the lifecycle with explicit learning.
entryCriteria: Replacement, migration, or end-of-life obligations are known
exitCriteria: Users, data, integrations, environments, and operational ownership are safely transitioned or closed
Required records and lessons are retained

stages.name: Retirement Decision & Plan
stages.objective: Define why, when, and how the service will be retired.

tasks.name: Approve retirement scope and plan
steps: Confirm business, technical, legal, security, and operational reasons for retirement.
Define replacement, user communication, compatibility, rollback, and exit criteria.
Assign owners and schedule decision checkpoints.
exitCriteria: Approve retirement scope and plan evidence is recorded
validationRules: The plan identifies affected stakeholders, dependencies, and irreversible actions
tasks.progressEvidence: Approve retirement scope and plan decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Migrate and Decommission
stages.objective: Move or dispose of data, users, integrations, infrastructure, and operational obligations safely.

tasks.name: Execute migration and data disposition
steps: Execute migration, archival, retention, deletion, or export according to approved policy.
Validate completeness, confidentiality, integrity, and recoverability where required.
Record final data and integration evidence.
exitCriteria: Execute migration and data disposition evidence is recorded
validationRules: No data or integration is silently abandoned
tasks.progressEvidence: Execute migration and data disposition decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

tasks.name: Decommission service and access
steps: Disable traffic, scheduled work, credentials, access paths, alerts, and environments in the approved order.
Verify replacement ownership and customer communication.
Retain required source, model, trace, release, incident, and decision records.
exitCriteria: Decommission service and access evidence is recorded
validationRules: Decommission evidence covers runtime, data, access, cost, and support surfaces
tasks.progressEvidence: Decommission service and access decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

stages.name: Closure & Organizational Learning
stages.objective: Close the lifecycle and feed reusable learning into future method profiles and product planning.

tasks.name: Complete closure review
steps: Confirm retirement exit criteria and records are complete.
Review product, architecture, operational, and method outcomes.
Publish reusable patterns, risks, and method changes for future projects.
exitCriteria: Complete closure review evidence is recorded
validationRules: Closure identifies retained evidence, unresolved obligations, and accountable custodians
tasks.progressEvidence: Complete closure review decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

workflows.name: Cross-Level Change Propagation
workflows.trigger: A model change at any level must propagate through CIM → PIM → PSM → artifacts.
steps: Complete level-local change workflow and EVL gate for the source level.
Run Impact Analysis on TraceModel: list downstream TraceLinks with reduced confidence.
Re-run ETL for affected level pair (cim-to-pim, pim-to-awspsm) with merge strategy.
Replay refinement phases on target level for impacted increment slice only.
Regenerate M2T artifacts; run end-to-end validation suite.
Record ManualDecision for human resolution items; update readiness assessments.

workflows.name: Post-Transform CIM Change
workflows.trigger: CIM must change after PIM or PSM already exists for this project.
steps: Freeze downstream models or branch increment.
Apply CIM change with full impact analysis.
Re-run CIM EVL and readiness gate.
Re-execute CIM→PIM ETL; reconcile PIM trace links and manual decisions.
Propagate to PSM and artifacts per end-to-end change workflow.

workflows.name: Post-Transform PIM Change
workflows.trigger: PIM must change after PSM or artifacts exist.
steps: Apply PIM change with impact analysis on trace links to CIM and PSM.
Re-run PIM EVL and readiness.
Re-execute PIM→PSM ETL; review platform mapping deltas.
Regenerate M2T artifacts; run deployment dry-run.

workflows.name: Post-M2T PSM Change
workflows.trigger: PSM changes after artifacts were generated or deployed.
steps: Apply PSM model change at owning phase.
Re-run PSM EVL and integration views.
Regenerate M2T artifacts; diff against prior generation.
Run CI validation and staged deployment.
